findings.title: Prisma crash-loop claim not corroborated by prisma-client-python source
findings.body: Comment claims an unpinned install 'grabs latest prisma-client-python, whose generated prisma/types.py no longer exports DatasourceOverride, breaking prisma.client's own import.' Direct inspection of RobertCraigie/prisma-client-py tags v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 (latest on PyPI) shows DatasourceOverride is exported in every version checked — from v0.13.0 onward it's implemented as `DatasourceOverride = _types.DatasourceOverride` (an alias to a class in the static _types.py) rather than a locally-defined class, but the name and the `from .types import DatasourceOverride` import in client.py.jinja both still resolve correctly at v0.15.0. This doesn't mean the pin is wrong (0.11.0 is still a valid choice), but the specific mechanism cited as the crash cause does not hold up against the current released source — it's possible Grok observed a transient/dev-build breakage rather than something reproducible on any tagged release.

findings.title: Prisma comment misattributes an exact pin to the wrong upstream extras group
findings.body: Comment says the pin matches 'litellm[proxy]'s own `prisma==0.11.0` requirement (extra-proxy)'. Checked litellm's pyproject.toml at main and tags v1.84.0→v1.98.0: prisma is not part of the `proxy` extra at all (only `fastapi` etc. live there); it's in a separate `extra_proxy` optional-dependency group, which in current/recent releases (≥~1.90, including 1.98.0 — the version this Dockerfile's unbounded `litellm[proxy]>=1.83.7` will actually resolve to) declares `prisma>=0.11.0,<1.0`, a range, not an exact pin. The literal `prisma==0.11.0` string only exists in litellm's `proxy-dev` PEP 735 [dependency-groups] entry — a dev/test-tooling group not installed by `pip install litellm[proxy]` at all. The comment conflates these two distinct, differently-scoped upstream declarations.

findings.title: FastAPI crash-loop root cause already worked around upstream in the litellm version this pin actually targets
findings.body: The get_flat_dependant removal-in-0.141.0 claim is independently verified accurate (confirmed present in fastapi 0.140.0/0.140.1, absent from 0.141.0/0.141.1 via direct source diff). However, litellm's own source at 1.98.0 (the version actually installed today given the unbounded `litellm[proxy]>=1.83.7` floor) no longer calls `get_flat_dependant` anywhere — litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/common.py switched to `fastapi.dependencies.utils.get_flat_params` specifically because 'fastapi>=0.140.7 removed get_flat_dependant()' (per litellm's own inline comment), and get_flat_params has been present since fastapi 0.136.3. So for the litellm version this Dockerfile will resolve today, the crash this pin guards against may already be moot upstream — the pin is still harmless (0.140.0 satisfies litellm's own fastapi>=0.136.3,<1.0 range and has get_flat_params), just possibly no longer load-bearing for its stated reason.

remaining_risks: No live container build/start was performed in this audit (out of stated scope) to directly confirm or refute the crash-loop scenarios described in the comments.

Both pins are hard `==` with no upper-bound flexibility; nothing in this diff schedules a revisit when litellm/fastapi/prisma move forward, so the image is frozen on these exact versions indefinitely unless someone manually bumps them.

Comment accuracy issues (F1/F2) suggest the investigation behind this PR may not have been fully validated against released upstream source — worth a quick confirmatory container build/run before treating this as fully closed.
